source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក (Techniques for Banana Cultivation), 2019, section II.1 (ការពង្រីកពូជ)
text: Banana can be multiplied in a few different ways. The traditional and by far most common method for farmers is to use suckers (offshoots, ក្នើង) that naturally sprout from the base of an established mother plant's corm; this is fast, simple, and produces plants genetically identical to the parent. Where a farmer wants to multiply planting material more intensively from a small number of good mother plants, cutting the corm into pieces, each with at least one healthy bud, is a way to obtain more planting units from one clump, though this requires more careful handling to prevent rot and disease entry at the cut surfaces. Tissue culture (laboratory micro-propagation) is also mentioned as a modern option for producing large numbers of uniform, disease-free plantlets, mainly used at a commercial or institutional scale rather than by individual smallholders. Seed propagation is possible for seeded types but is rarely used commercially since the resulting plants can vary from the parent and take longer to establish; nearly all Cambodian farmers rely on vegetative propagation via suckers.
